CONTEXT AND OBJECTIVES
Wealthsimple’s (“WS”) recent product announcements have garnered interest and attention across FIs and consumers on its offerings and value proposition
Given the attention, this fact-base was developed with the objectives to: 1) outline WS’s growth and impact on BNS; 2) understand their relative strengths, and 3) frame next steps and discuss if a further strategic response is required
WEALTHSIMPLE GROWTH STORY
Since its inception, WS has experienced strong growth; it now has ~3MM clients and has seen ~70% CAGR in assets since 2018 (vs. 8% for BNS and 4% for TNG) 
While outflows to WS across Retail, iTRADE and TNG account for 2% of total, net outflows to WS have grown by ~100% Y/Y and are overindexed from primary clients (~50% of outflows) 
Clients sending funds to WS skew younger and less affluent (e.g., clients aged 18–34 make up ~70% of WS outflow activity, despite representing only ~35% of our total client base)
WS leads the market in net switching-gains across most banking and investing products; BNS leads in GIC net-switching gains, and TNG is top three in chequing accts and RRSPs
Continued net outflows to WS could reduce our assets by $60-230Bn in next five years (~$0.2-1.2Bn impact on F30 run-rate revenue) and our primary clients by 5-20% of today’s base 
WEALTHSIMPLE STRENGTHS
Through primary and secondary research, Wealthsimple’s strengths have been identified along the following dimensions: 
Products: WS has strong direct investing and retail investing offerings (e.g., robo); WS continues to evolve its offering to meet client needs (e.g., banking) 
Pricing: WS offers value for money in the form of low cost, high rates; additionally, WS offers incentives and promotions with high rewards 
Experience: WS has created strong brand equity among its clients through its digital capabilities, branding, and two-way client engagement 
Enablers: WS’s ability to execute at pace can be attributed to their modern tech stack, agile delivery, calculated risk-taking culture, and long-term profitability horizon
PATH FORWARD
Near-term, WS will likely deepen its wealth and banking offerings; Medium-to-long-term, IPO is the likely destination for WS, allowing Power Corp. to unlock value from its stake
Across BNS and Tangerine, there are several strategies and investments in-flight that are expected to combat outflows to WS (e.g., Retail segmentation, iTRADE growth strategy, Project Clarity); time and resources are required to execute on these initiatives and realize benefits
Specifically, the highest priority initiatives to compete are:  
Tangerine ‘Project Clarity’ strategy, including the crypto offering
CX initiatives within CB and Wealth, particularly the digital experience
At this time, these initiatives are moving as quickly as possible; no further action is needed but we will continue to monitor progress
